core.text: Remove the preferred operating dependency: sustained commanded 900 rpm coupled to three successful optical checks. Use commanded 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds; stop regardless of images, with no later stirring or feedback restart before second-120 sampling. This construction retains rotation but removes both high-speed operation and optical control of duration.

One stipulated trial already supports a bounded counterexample: early 300 rpm image spreads exceeded 4 percent, yet stopping at second 60 yielded final vial readings 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. Reliable repeat success remains hypothetical. Matched 900 rpm final samples and total stirring duration are absent; neither comparative uniformity nor time savings is established.

Propose up to six fresh-recipe repeats using 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye, a rinsed vessel, one dye bottle, fixed addition location, locked camera and spill tray; stop if liquid escapes. Record five-second images without controlling operation. After stopping at second 60, sample at second 120: withdraw 1 mL at each of 10, 28 and 45 mm within ten seconds, alternating depth order across paired repeats. Report raw attenuation, normalized spread, commanded speed, duration and every target failure against common references.

residue.text: A stronger future deprivation hypothesis removes magnetic rotation entirely: precommit six low-position 20 mL withdrawals and upper-side returns within 60 seconds, then the same quiet interval and depth sampling. This syringe-only construction is unobserved, may disturb gradients, and must occupy trials within the six-trial cap rather than expand it. It is an alternative experiment, not an established substitute.

Transient specks do not identify bubbles; common-aliquot repeatability does not calibrate concentration. Successful final samples establish only the bounded attenuation proxy after cessation and sampling. They cannot establish earlier uniformity, explain 900 rpm fluctuations, or generalize to other liquids or vessels.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds reliably achieves the final sample proxy; high-speed optical stabilization is dispensable in this recipe.
tension.account_b: Incompatible rival hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds generally leaves depth gradients; the stipulated success was exceptional or sampling-mediated.
tension.prediction_a: Repeated fixed-intervention trials yield final spread at most 4 percent, including trials with earlier image failures, without systematic dependence on sampling order.
tension.prediction_b: Repeated identical trials generally yield final spread above 4 percent, or apparent success depends systematically on sampling order. Failure alone would not establish necessity of 900 rpm or its optical rule.
